executive_summary: Mechanical closure is complete on the fingerprint the packet records: judge coverage over the run scope is complete, judge closure is closed, workflow-owned blockers are zero, there are no deferrals and no terminal unresolved resolutions, so the readiness verdict is publishable-pending-owner-approval and only the owner's actions remain (personal mathematical audit, deliberate status:published changes, push/deployment). Every recorded fatal defect row carries disposition fixed, covering this run's fresh adjudication and cross-batch findings, a repeat-round citation finding, and a large block of historical Step-7 findings imported as recorded evidence rather than re-adjudicated here. The residual risk is therefore mathematical, not procedural: fresh fatals cluster at proof-step locations and in inference, hypothesis, statement and citation classes; repeated repairs concentrate on a stable set of items; and the configured judge set is single-model, so adjudicated outcomes carry the entire weight of rejected verdicts. The reading priorities and recommendations below interpret the packet's receipts; they are not an independent re-verification of any item.
caveats: A large block of the fatal rows are historical Step-7 records whose note states they were imported from their exact matching original report with no new adjudication or independent audit; their certification rests on carried evidence plus the recorded repair, so treat them as spot-check candidates rather than freshly re-verified content.

Fresh fatal findings are dominated by proof-step locations and by inference, hypothesis, statement and citation classes (unlicensed or invalid inference, missing hypotheses, false or overstrong claims, citation-inaccurate facts blocks, ill-formed formulas); the residual risk sits in repaired proof, statement and facts text because every fatal row is already disposed fixed.

Judge coverage is complete for the configured set, but that set resolves to a single model with no mixed verdicts and no null responses; no cross-model corroboration exists, so the adjudicated outcomes — confirmed fatal, confirmed nonfatal and false positive — carry the entire weight of every rejected judge verdict.

The touch ledger lists a substantial set of items repaired more than once, including ex-smooth-conic-is-projective-line-with-point, lem-surface-green-identity-on-smooth-bordered-domain and prop-rigidity-in-rauch-comparison at three recorded repairs each, and every subject that carries both an imported historical fatal row and a fresh fatal row also appears in that repeated-repair list; repeated repair is the packet's strongest fragility signal.

Adjudication resolved a small number of judge rejections as false positives; those items were deliberately left unchanged, so their text contains no repair for the original objection and should not be mistaken for an unaddressed defect.

The fatal ledger includes false-boundary-disposition rows (one an order definition's empty-domain case) and several missing-hypothesis rows, so conventions for empty, zero, endpoint and degenerate inputs in the repaired definitions and statements deserve explicit owner attention.

The packet's item-kind histogram splits four kinds into quoted and unquoted variants because the evidence tool captures the frontmatter kind token verbatim and a small set of scoped item files quote the YAML scalar (for example thm-abelian-k-zero-agrees-with-bounded-derived-k-zero and lem-triangulated-k-zero-shifts-and-exact-functors); this is a metadata-rendering quirk of the histogram, not a content defect.

This interpretation is bound to the packet's receipts, hashes and frozen context; I did not independently re-read or re-verify the mathematics of any item, so nothing here substitutes for the owner's personal mathematical audit, and any later content edit invalidates the current judge evidence for the edited item.
